chunks: As for what Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated from Ibn al-Mughirah, from Mansur, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
The blood-money of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian is the blood-money of the Muslim.

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: the Christian; a member of the Christian community
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيِّ: the Magian; a member of the Zoroastrian community
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِ: the Muslim; here, the standard of comparison for diyah
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيِّ: the Jew; a member of the Jewish community
key_terms.دِيَةُ: blood-money; the prescribed financial compensation for unlawful killing or injury

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the diyah of Jews, Christians, and Magians compared to Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning blood-money, declaring that the diyah of a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian is the same as the diyah of a Muslim. It pertains to judicial and compensatory rulings in cases involving protected non-Muslim communities.
